title: CDots@PMoA/ZnO/PVP Hybrid Films with Enhanced Visible-Light Photochromic Performance
content: Incorporating photochromic materials into rewritable paper enables light-based printing, reducing both the pollution associated with papermaking and that arising from ink use. Most existing photochromic materials respond primarily to ultraviolet (UV) light, and printing systems employing UV lasers are substantially more expensive than visible-light-based inkless printing systems. In this study, a visible-light-responsive CDots-doped PMoA/ZnO/PVP composite system was developed and used to fabricate rewritable printing paper. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy revealed changes in morphology and local chemical structure upon composite formation and visible-light irradiation. The hybrid films changed from colorless to blue under visible light, and the incorporation of carbon dots (CDots) enhanced their photochromic performance. Visible-light excitation induced photoreduction through the transfer of photogenerated electrons and protons, reducing Mo⁶⁺ to Mo⁵⁺ and forming heteropoly blue species. Rewritable inkless printing paper prepared from the CDots@PMoA/ZnO/PVP composite solution produced clearly legible text, and the printed patterns remained clear through repeated erasing and rewriting cycles, demonstrating good stability.
